sections.title: The promised engagement includes exposure to an audience
sections.cue: What did the parties understand the performer would receive?
paragraphs: The assigned account concerns a theatrical engagement at the Hippodrome. The quoted judicial passage says both contracting parties knew the plaintiff would receive billing and advertising for that appearance, and that such publicity had value in the theatrical profession.
The opportunity therefore offered more than salary alone. Appearing before an audience and being advertised as doing so could promote the performer’s professional career.

sources.pinpoint: Assigned judicial quotation; C&M printed 1035, The Right to Work

sections.title: Withheld work raises a question about the additional promised benefit
sections.cue: Why does payment of wages not by itself exhaust the inquiry?
paragraphs: The textbook introduces the case while asking what a performer loses when promised work is withheld and whether recovery might extend beyond contractual salary. In the supplied passage, publicity was an anticipated product of the engagement known to both sides, not simply a personal hope developed later by the employee.
That connection explains the additional contractual interest at stake. The quotation does not reproduce the court’s complete treatment of foreseeability, proof or the value of the lost opportunity.

sections.title: The excerpt leaves the amount and complete judgment unresolved
sections.cue: What cannot be inferred from the surrounding editorial comparison?
paragraphs: The surrounding note compares decisions discussing harm to reputation with concerns about uncertainty and unforeseeability. The Oliver quotation itself identifies valuable billing and advertising; it does not establish compensation for injured feelings or all later reputational consequences.

The complete engagement terms, pleaded claims, trial findings, appellate sequence and damages judgment remain unavailable, as do the judges and any separate writings. The assigned passage supports recognition of the promised professional opportunity, but supplies no verified final award to recount.
